question: When does a small residual imply a small solution error, and which norm controls amplification?
entry: Exact canonical prerequisites2.3 and2.5: matrix maps/inverses and SVD; no2.6 dependency imported.
exit: Prove induced-norm submultiplicativity and condition-dependent residual/data/matrix perturbation bounds; distinguish sensitivity from solver failure.
assumptions: Euclidean vector norms and their induced operator norms in orthonormal coordinates; Frobenius separately labeled
Square invertible linear system; nonzero b and x for relative ratios, absolute bounds used for zero b
Combined matrix perturbation requires eta=norm(A inverse)*norm(E)<1; sufficient not necessary condition
Exact sensitivity cases constructed deliberately, not observed solver failures; no2.6 dependency imported

symbols.A,B,x,b: Matrix maps, solution and right-hand side
symbols.op,F: Induced spectral norm versus Frobenius norm; TQI convention difference explicit
symbols.kappa,sigma_min,sigma_max: Relative normwise condition number and extremal singular values
symbols.xhat,e,r: Candidate, forward error xhat-x and residual b-A*xhat
symbols.E,f,Delta x: Matrix/right-hand perturbations and exact solution change
symbols.eta,epsilon_A,epsilon_b,delta: Smallness parameter, relative input norms and binary scale

proof_obligations: Induced operator norm equals largest singular value and bounds every matrix-vector product
Norm properties and compatible submultiplicativity derived from vector norms
Frobenius contrast and op<=F via rowwise Cauchy–Schwarz
Inverse norm1/sigma_min and relative kappa ratio for square invertible matrices
Absolute and relative right-hand input sensitivity and residual-to-forward-error bound
Exact binary diagonal counterexample attains kappa times relative residual
Matrix-vector product perturbation includes cross term
eta<1 guarantees perturbed invertibility using lower gain and SVD; full combined solution error bound derived
Uniform scaling, zero right-hand-side and singular threshold boundaries separated
